pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/57072

Feature added recently in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/105841

Replaced workaround from https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/48892. `ServerWebSocket` -> `AbortStream`. Solves the same issue but in a different way. This is verified by the test `WebSocket_Abort_Interrupts_Pending_ReceiveAsync`

The `AbortStream` workaround handles the background keep alive which `ServerWebSocket` did not. The old workaround only worked when someone called Abort on **our** websocket impl (`ServerWebSocket`), which can only happen in user code. With the addition of an abort call from inside the runtimes websocket impl, our `ServerWebSocket.Abort` function would never be called for keep alive timeouts.

issue_context.title: WebSocket keep-alive timeout API
issue_context.body:
## Background and Motivation

<!--
We welcome API proposals! We have a process to evaluate the value and shape of new API. There is an overview of our process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/APIReviewProcess.md). This template will help us gather the information we need to start the review process.
First, please describe the purpose and value of the new API here.
-->
dotnet/runtime is adding an API to control the keep-alive timeout see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/48729#issuecomment-1979542776
Our WebSocket middleware exposes options to control the websocket options being used so we would want to expose an equivalent option.

## Proposed API

```diff
namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;

public class WebSocketOptions
{
    public TimeSpan KeepAliveInterval { get; set; }
+   public TimeSpan KeepAliveTimeout { get; set; }
}
```

## Usage Examples

```csharp
builder.AddWebSockets(o =>
{
    o.KeepAliveTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
});
```

## Alternative Designs

How does this compare to analogous APIs in other ecosystems and libraries?
-->

What's the distinction between KeepAliveInterval and KeepAliveTimeout?

KeepAliveInterval determined how often a Pong is sent to the other side. However, with the introduction of KeepAliveTimeout, if the value of KeepAliveTimeout is non-zero and non-infinite then KeepAliveInterval is how often a Ping is sent, and KeepAliveTimeout is how long we wait for a Pong response before closing the connection due to a timeout.

Background: a Pong is a Ping for which no response/acknowledgement is expected

To paraphrase:

A KeepAliveInterval of 5 seconds with no (i.e. zero or infinite) KeepAliveTimeout means "send a Pong every 5 seconds".

A KeepAliveInterval of 5 seconds with a KeepAliveTimeout of 1 second means "send a Ping every 5 seconds and kill the connection if any ping acknowledgement (i.e. Pong) takes more than 1 second".

Is that right?
I think another way to look at it would be that a keep alive frame with no timeout has no reason to look for a response, so it degrades from a Ping to a Pong?

- What are the default values?
    - We can, but don't have to, use the same ones as runtime
- We also have KestrelServerLimits.KeepAliveTimeout
    - It doesn't accept 0
    - It defaults to 130 seconds
- What value do we use to express that there is no timeout?
    - MaxValue?
    - 0?
    - Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan?
- Validate with a test that passing MaxValue doesn't break things (regardless of whether it means no timeout)
- A comment on the runtime PR suggests it was Ping before it was Pong


```diff
namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;

public class WebSocketOptions
{
    public TimeSpan KeepAliveInterval { get; set; }
+   public TimeSpan KeepAliveTimeout { get; set; }
}
```

API Approved!

review_comments: Can we add a test showing `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` and `TimeSpan.Zero` are allowed and both disable the timeout?

Idk how to test that they disable the timeout though. That's internal to the websocket impl, we'd need to use HttpClient to receive messages and then write a WebSocket frame parser to inspect the messages. And testing for a lack of Ping message from the server means just waiting for some arbitrary amount of time to check if we didn't get a message.
I'm moderately amused that `InfiniteTimeSpan` is less than `Zero`.
You can still do it using different syntax, but you lose most of the benefits.
I figured you'd always get a `ConnectionAbortedException` if the read is canceled by `HttpContext.Abort()`. Is it ever really a `WebSocketException`?

Yes, if the WebSocket.ReceiveAsync call occurs after the timeout. It's a race, we could reduce the chance by changing KeepAliveTimeout to a larger value, but then the test would take longer 😄 
And would still technically be a flaky test.
Should we update this to match `WebSocketAcceptContext.KeepAliveInterval` or vice-versa?
